stem: A car moves on a level circular road of radius $40$ m. The coefficient of friction between the tyres and road is $0.50$. As shown in the figure, what is the maximum speed without slipping? Take $g = 10$ m s$^{-2}$.
notes: from question bank g17a0d8353176 (verified in job 20261127-132429-aa8a)
working:
At the limiting speed, $f=\mu N$ and $N=mg$.
$\dfrac{mv^2}{r}=f=\mu mg$
$v=\sqrt{\mu rg}=\sqrt{0.50(40)(10)}=10\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$

Independent check: On a level road, friction supplies centripetal force: μmg = mv²/r. Thus v = √(μgr) = √(0.50 × 10 × 40) = 10√2 m s⁻¹.
solution:
On a level road, friction provides the centripetal force; at the limiting speed, $f=\mu mg$.
$$\frac{mv^2}{r}=\mu mg \quad\Rightarrow\quad v=\sqrt{\mu rg}=\sqrt{0.50\times40\times10}=10\sqrt{2}\ \text{m s}^{-1}$$
